messages:
maya: Quick runtime follow-ups from todays roadmap Q&A.
maya: KV eviction question: can tenants set hard residency bounds or only global heuristics?
taylor: Plan: Private gets per-tenant hard caps first, Dedicated gets soft-TTLs + optional hard cap. Hosted stays global by default.
alex: Soft-TTL = mark low-priority but keep in cache briefly; reduces p99 tail when bursts end.
rami: Batching metric: which percentile should autoscaling use? p99, p99.5, or p99.9?
taylor: Autoscaler will offer p99.5 by default, ops can opt into p99.9 windows. Console shows p50/p90/p99/p99.9.
sre-bot: [notice] High-cardinality tagging for batch metrics is sampled at 1% by default.
maya: Kernel pinning: can customers pin kernels in Dedicated/Private?
taylor: Yes. Dedicated alpha supports kernel_profile in manifest. Private supports operator-managed pinning. We provide compatibility checks.
alex: Fallback order: pinned -> compatible-quantized -> generic. Customers can opt to disable fallbacks if they want strict pinning.
rami: Rollout policy: auto-rollback for perf regressions?
taylor: Auto-rollback requires crossing latency SLO delta AND higher error rate. Cost-only wins need manual review.
maya: Prewarm improvements for KV-heavy cold starts?
alex: We snapshot hot KV to disk and opportunistically rehydrate on start. Internal tests show ~30% cold-path improvement.
maya: Request: please publish a short RFC + migration checklist so support can answer enterprise queries.
taylor: Will publish RFC and migration guide next week and post link here.
maya: Thanks all. :thumbsup:
